evidence.claim: TARGET T1 (window exists): CONFIRMED. Between gate 9 (payload-digest validation of the SOURCE payload, install.py:385-392) and the copy that consumes it (install.py:438-448), the install runs gate 10 (SBOM), gate 11 (license), gate 12 (dependencies -- which recursively installs and can take arbitrary wall-clock) and gate 13a (lockfile pin). report.question: Is there a window between the validator reading a package and the installer consuming it in which the bytes can change, and does the installer re-verify the hash it validated?
report.answer: YES there is a window (gates 10/11/12/13a run between the gate-9 payload validation and the copy; dependency installs make it arbitrarily long and the source bytes are not snapshotted), BUT the installer re-verifies the digest of the ACTUALLY-INSTALLED copy at the point of use (install.py:449-450) and refuses (MKT-I09) on any mismatch. Measured: a byte swapped right after gate-9 is caught by the SBOM gate (MKT-I10); a byte swapped at the copy seam is caught by the post-copy digest re-check (MKT-I09); in both, install is REFUSED and zero bytes are left in the site. The swapped bytes install ONLY when that post-copy re-check is deleted (mutant SUCCESS, malicious digest), proving the re-verification is the load-bearing defense. So a PASSED check still describes the bytes that get installed: the classic validate-then-install TOCTOU is CLOSED for the installed payload. Not-a-duplicate of ADV-0028 (which asks whether the signature check can be SKIPPED).
